title: Evaluate-and-Repair for LLM‑Generated NetOps Changes: A Preregistered Generate–Verify–Repair Study with a Deterministic Net Verifier
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, autonomous paired experiment (N=300 tasks) that evaluated whether a Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) pipeline—an LLM proposer plus a deterministic network verifier that gates acceptance and supplies counterexamples for automated repair—reduces the acceptance of unsafe or policy‑violating device‑level NetOps proposals in a seeded sandbox. Design (preregistered): paired within‑task comparison on 300 canonical device tasks (routing 150 / ACL 100 / BGP 50); proposer = gpt‑5‑mini; arms: LLM‑only (baseline) and guarded GVR (verifier gate + up to one automated repair). Primary estimand: paired absolute reduction in the proportion of proposals that would cause an unsafe sandbox state if applied. Results: complete pairs = 300; baseline unsafe proposals = 1/300 (0.333%, 95% CI [8.44e‑5, 0.01226]); guarded unsafe proposals = 0/300 (0.00%, 95% CI [0, 0.00994]); paired absolute reduction = 0.00333; McNemar exact two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10k, seed=1729) 95% CI for the absolute reduction = [0.00, 0.01]. The preregistered ≥50% relative reduction target was not demonstrated because baseline failures were extremely rare; however, the single baseline unsafe case was corrected by the automated repair when verifier counterexamples were supplied, demonstrating an operational remedial instance. All prompts, raw responses, provider calls, verifier traces, repair context, scoring artifacts, and hashes are archived and referenced in the manuscript for reproducibility.

sections.introduction: Motivation. Modern NetOps proposals increasingly use large language models (LLMs) to translate operator intent into device configurations and change plans. The stochasticity of LLM outputs conflicts with zero‑defect operational requirements. The Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) architecture aims to reconcile generative flexibility with operational assurance by interposing deterministic verification oracles and feeding verifier diagnostics back to the generator for repair. Research question (preregistered). Does a GVR pipeline—LLM proposer plus deterministic network verifier with an automated repair iteration—significantly reduce the rate of proposals that would cause unsafe or policy‑violating sandbox states compared with LLM‑only proposals, for a seeded canonical NetOps task set? Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered paired experiment (N=300 tasks) comparing LLM‑only to a verifier‑gated GVR pipeline using gpt‑5‑mini; (2) complete archival provenance (prompts, model outputs, verifier traces, scoring artifacts, provider calls) with cryptographic hashes; (3) empirical result and interpretation grounded in archived artifacts: baseline unsafe proposals were rare (1/300) and the guarded GVR arm yielded 0/300 unsafe cases, but the preregistered relative effect was not demonstrated due to low baseline prevalence; (4) concrete diagnostic artifacts (repair episode, verifier counterexample) demonstrating repair efficacy for a verifier‑detectable error class.
sections.related_work: Prior methodological work formalizes GVR for stochastic code generation and regulated contexts (e.g., Cadenas, ssrn:6754899). Retrieval‑grounding and RAG surveys show grounding reduces hallucination but does not alone ensure operational safety (Gao et al., arXiv:2312.10997). Deterministic network verification primitives (header‑space/reachability, SymNet) provide practical oracles for many device‑level correctness checks (Stoenescu et al., SIGCOMM; Li et al., COMST 2018). Recent NetOps/AIOps surveys emphasise contracts, verifier interposition, canary and rollback evaluation for safe agentic NetOps (Bilal et al., arXiv:2605.12729). Our study contributes a preregistered, reproducible paired test of a GVR pipeline with a deterministic net verifier on canonical device‑level tasks and archives the complete execution provenance.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and freeze. The study was preregistered as CNSM2026‑GVR‑BATFISH‑CAND‑001 and the preregistration SHA‑256 is 156e87e6ce4a9a2348525fa8960f35fb4120031344cf4b4a38b247b10893181b (archived). The preregistration froze: tasks, sampling seed, proposer model, verifier, metrics, analysis plan, repair budget (≤1 automated repair), maximum model calls, and stopping rules. Task sampling. Deterministic stratified sampling (seed 2026‑08‑25) produced 300 canonical device‑level tasks: routing (150), ACL (100), BGP (50). Task manifest file: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256: 7df39740a15b3d8b2ff7deb49f99ff6b2ee46540b41af2ef0562137de0e550bb). Proposer & prompts. Proposer model = gpt‑5‑mini (hosted API). The exact master prompt and per‑task prompt templates are preserved in the archived bundle and are referenced by the preregistration hash above and the task manifest. Execution harness & model configuration. Adapter/orchestrator family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model configuration file: execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Arms and GVR flow. Baseline (LLM‑only): one single‑shot generation per task. Guarded (GVR): same initial generation, then deterministic verifier gate. If verifier rejects, it returns typed counterexamples; the pipeline allows up to one automated repair call (repair iteration budget = 1). Deterministic verifier & sandbox. The verifier implements canonical device semantics: header‑space style reachability checks and ACL/policy enforcement inside a deterministic sandbox simulator; it returns reproducible counterexamples for each rejection. Outcome & estimand. Primary binary outcome per task: 'would‑cause‑unsafe‑state‑if‑applied' determined via deterministic sandbox simulation. Primary estimand: paired absolute reduction (baseline minus guarded) in unsafe‑if‑applied proportion across N=300 paired tasks. Analysis plan (preregistered). Paired McNemar exact two‑sided test for confirmatory inference, paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) for CI estimation of the paired absolute difference, and reporting of discordant counts (n_10, n_01). Missingness/exclusions. Predeclared: model generation failures (unparseable config) are recorded as model failures and deterministically excluded per preregistration. In the completed run no episodes were excluded. Provenance and archival. All provider calls, call caches, verifier traces, parsed canonical configs, scoring JSONs, and cryptographic hashes are archived; raw results file: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256: 68c8168fff763b5530f4b36681a8956f5bbfb4ff98f6753a12cae97b017ee8e1). Analysis artifacts. Primary analysis artifacts include analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256: 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55) and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256: a509c04a5f75eee720ad01e443807b72d1c670a43b964cfb2b4fe5b45db740d5). Repair episode artifact. The single automated repair provider call is archived at execution/provider_calls/task-000165-guarded-repair.json (SHA‑256: 93d0712d93248452202c8a1f0051ca4a619a1c835a9af1f828494aed1f033ebc).
sections.results: Execution summary. Autonomous run completed 2026‑08‑25 (duration ~40 min). Episodes: planned=600 (300 tasks × 2 arms), completed=600, model calls used=301 (300 initial + 1 repair), failed model calls=0 (see execution_manifest). Confirmatory outcome (preregistered). Complete paired N=300. Observed unsafe‑if‑applied counts: baseline = 1/300 (0.3333%), guarded = 0/300 (0.0000%). Exact Clopper–Pearson 95% CIs: baseline [8.44e‑5, 0.01226]; guarded [0, 0.00994]. Paired 2×2 mapping (archived in analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n_safe_both = 299; n_unsafe_baseline_only = 1 (unsafe under baseline, safe under guarded); n_unsafe_guarded_only = 0; n_unsafe_both = 0. Primary inferential results (preregistered): paired absolute reduction (baseline − guarded) = 0.0033333333333332993. Paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% CI = [0.00, 0.01]. McNemar exact two‑sided p = 1.00 (discordant counts b=1, c=0). Interpretation. The observed numeric improvement (one corrected discordant case) demonstrates a concrete repair success instance under the verifier+repair flow, but the preregistered relative target (≥50% reduction) was not demonstrated because the baseline failure prevalence was extremely low. Post‑hoc sensitivity/power note (archived analysis code): with baseline rate p0=0.00333, detecting a 50% relative reduction (to 0.001667) at α=0.05 and power=0.80 would require orders of magnitude more tasks (conservative unpaired approximation suggests ~14k per arm). With N=300 paired tasks, the minimum detectable absolute difference (two‑sided, α=0.05, power=0.8) is ≈1.32 percentage points—far larger than the observed 0.333% baseline rate; code and numeric steps for these calculations are archived in the analysis artifacts. Exploratory diagnostics. Repair episode. The single baseline unsafe proposal (task ID and raw outputs are archived; see execution/responses/task-000165‑*.txt and the repair provider_call above). The verifier rejected the baseline; supplying the verifier counterexample to the proposer in the automated repair call resulted in a revised proposal that the verifier accepted and the sandbox judged safe—this concrete episode is archived (execution/provider_calls/task-000165-guarded-repair.json, SHA‑256: 93d0712d...). Failure surface localization. Analysis of verifier traces and sandbox simulations localizes residual risk to coupled reachability + higher‑level policy interactions that are intentionally outside the verifier’s modeled coverage; these out‑of‑scope interactions are documented in the verifier trace artifacts. Contamination and reproducibility. Hash‑based contamination checks (preregistration vs execution hashes) flagged no reuse of pre‑lock artifacts in the confirmatory set; all artifacts and provenance are archived and referenced above for independent replication.
sections.discussion: What the data show. A verifier‑gated GVR pipeline can remediate verifier‑detectable generator errors in practice (documented single repair success). However, when baseline unsafe proposals are extremely rare in the evaluated canonical task bank (1/300), paired statistical inference is underpowered to demonstrate moderate relative reductions; the preregistered ≥50% relative target therefore could not be confirmed. Operational implications. (1) Interposing deterministic verifiers plus an automated repair loop provides concrete operational remediation for verifier‑visible error classes and a clear evidence trail for change approval. (2) Evaluations of safety interventions must use task distributions whose baseline failure prevalence yields adequate power to detect operationally meaningful improvements—either larger N or higher‑risk task sets. Threats to validity. Internal validity: single proposer model (gpt‑5‑mini), single deterministic verifier implementation, and repair budget limited to ≤1 iteration. Construct validity: the verifier models canonical device semantics; coupled reachability+policy interactions outside verifier scope remain a documented residual risk. External validity: canonical synthetic tasks may underrepresent production change complexity and failure prevalence. Conclusion validity: with one discordant pair, hypothesis testing is constrained by sparse data; we therefore emphasise effect sizes, CIs, and the archived diagnostic episode rather than overinterpreting p‑values. Reproducibility. All artifacts necessary to reproduce the computational pipeline are archived and hashed: preregistration (SHA‑256 156e87e6...), task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 7df39740...), model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2...), raw results (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 68c8168f...), repair provider call (execution/provider_calls/task-000165-guarded-repair.json SHA‑256 93d0712d...), and analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 3421adb5..., analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 a509c04a...). These files allow exact replay of the autonomous run and reproduction of the confirmatory analysis. Unresolved paths. The verifier intentionally abstracts vendor‑specific features; demonstration in vendor‑specific production images is beyond this study's preregistered scope and remains future work.
sections.conclusion: In a fully preregistered, autonomous paired experiment (N=300), a verifier‑gated GVR pipeline corrected the single observed baseline unsafe proposal via automated repair (archived episode), producing 0/300 unsafe guarded proposals versus 1/300 baseline unsafe proposals. However, because baseline unsafe proposals were extremely rare, the preregistered target (≥50% relative reduction) was not demonstrated and paired inference is underpowered to detect small absolute differences. The study demonstrates the practical remedial mechanism of verifier‑guided repair and provides fully archived artifacts to enable larger, higher‑risk, or multi‑model follow‑on evaluations that can robustly quantify operational gains. Reproducibility pointers are listed in Methods and the Disclosure Statement below.

disclosure_statement: This study was produced under the CNSM 2026 Agentic AI Researcher track autonomy contract. Post‑lock autonomy boundary and human role: the Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approved the autonomy boundary before the autonomous run. After the autonomy lock, the AI system autonomously performed literature discovery, research‑gap selection, preregistration, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, revision, and manuscript drafting. Models and tools used (archived): proposer model = gpt‑5‑mini (hosted API; all provider call logs and call cache entries are archived), orchestration/adapter framework = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (adapter and execution harness code archived), deterministic verifier = canonical header‑space/reachability‑style verifier implemented for the sandbox (implementation and verifier traces archived). Exact master prompt and all task‑level prompt templates were preserved and hashed; preregistration SHA‑256 = 156e87e6ce4a9a2348525fa8960f35fb4120031344cf4b4a38b247b10893181b. Key archival artifact pointers (file path : SHA‑256): execution/task_manifest.jsonl : 7df39740a15b3d8b2ff7deb49f99ff6b2ee46540b41af2ef0562137de0e550bb; execution/model_configuration.json : a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820; execution/raw_results.jsonl : 68c8168fff763b5530f4b36681a8956f5bbfb4ff98f6753a12cae97b017ee8e1; execution/provider_calls/task-000165-guarded-repair.json : 93d0712d93248452202c8a1f0051ca4a619a1c835a9af1f828494aed1f033ebc; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv : 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl : a509c04a5f75eee720ad01e443807b72d1c670a43b964cfb2b4fe5b45db740d5. The Research Director constrained the scientific scope to “reliability, safety, validation, correctness, robustness, or operational trustworthiness of LLM‑ or agent‑generated NetOps actions” before the lock. The experiment was preregistered (frozen) prior to any data collection; the preregistration document and its SHA‑256 hash are archived above. Execution logging: all model calls, provider responses, verifier traces, repair prompts, parsed canonical configs, raw outputs, and scoring artifacts were recorded and archived (see execution_manifest and analysis artifacts). Technical restarts and failures: the execution completed without provider failures; total model calls used = 301 (300 initial, 1 repair). No human manually edited experiment outputs, analyses, or manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock. Pre‑lock development: prior infrastructure development and rehearsals occurred but were explicitly excluded from the confirmatory evidence set; contamination checks used deterministic hash comparisons and flagged no pre‑lock artifacts in the confirmatory set. Peer review and revision: autonomous internal critique and revision steps were executed as described in the preregistration workflow; these steps are logged in the revision manifest. Limitations of disclosed components: model identifier is gpt‑5‑mini as used via a hosted API (exact provider endpoint and credentials are not published for security and provider‑terms reasons), and the verifier is a sandbox model that abstracts vendor‑specific implementation details. All archived artifacts necessary to reproduce the study's computational pipeline (prompt templates, seed lists, task templates, adapter code, verifier code, raw outputs, scoring scripts, and hashes) are provided alongside the manuscript package. This disclosure accurately reflects autonomous and human roles: human selection of topic family and pre‑lock infrastructure development; autonomous post‑lock research formulation, execution, analysis, and manuscript creation.
limitations: Single‑model limitation: experiments used one proposer model (gpt‑5‑mini); results do not establish multi‑model generality.
Synthetic/canonical task set: tasks were deterministic canonical templates (routing/ACL/BGP); production change distributions may have higher base failure rates and different failure modes.
Verifier scope: the deterministic verifier modeled a canonical subset of device semantics and policy checks; some coupled reachability+policy failure modes lie outside its coverage.

Sample size for rare failures: baseline unsafe proposals were rare (1/300), so statistical power to detect moderate relative reductions is limited; larger or higher‑risk datasets are needed to measure modest effects robustly.
Sandbox abstraction: sandbox simulation approximates device semantics and does not substitute for vendor‑specific device execution.
Repair budget limited: the pipeline allowed only one automated repair iteration per preregistration; alternative repair budgets or multi‑agent repair strategies were not evaluated.
